articles.title: Trump warns 'very big things' imminent: 'When do I blow the entire nation up?'
articles.description: President Donald Trump told Fox News’ Trey Yingst Sunday morning that, regarding speculation of an imminent U.S. escalation in the Middle East, “very big things” would take place in the “not-so-distant future,” things that include ‘wiping Iran out” entirely. Fears mounted Saturday night after Trump abruptly cut his weekend getaway in Maryland short and returned to the White House without explanation, a schedule change that came amid other signals that hinted at imminent U.S. military action. Yingst spoke to Trump by phone Sunday morning and was asked by Fox News’ “Fox & Friends Weekend” to provide viewers with the latest on the president’s thinking. “[Trump] tells Fox News he's in a 'deciding mode' and that 'very big things' are going to be happening in the 'not-so-distant future,’” Yingst said. “The president described the current choices on the table as 'wiping Iran out, letting them rot economically, or making a deal.’ He added, 'my question is, if and when do I blow the entire nation up, they better behave.'” Fox News’ Charles Hurt pressed Yingst for more details. “Can you give us any idea about what 'not-so-distant future' means?” Hurt asked. “Are we thinking hours, or we thinking days?” Yingst said it was “not clear at this moment,” with Iranian officials reportedly preparing for the United States to resume hostilities. Trump tells Fox he's in a "deciding mode" and that "very big things" to come in the "not-so-distant future." "If and when do I blow the entire nation up, they better behave" pic.twitter.com/URLKDgLhzX — Alexander Willis (@ReporterWillis) September 20, 2026

articles.title: KP CM Afridi blames deteriorating security situation on ‘failed’ foreign policy
articles.description: PESHAWAR: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Saturday said that the deteriorating security situation in the country was the result of a failed foreign policy pursued over the last 22 years. “If a policy is not delivering results and is continuously failing, there is a need to change it,” he said during a visit to Kohat. The chief minister met the families of the police personnel and civilians martyred in the terrorist attack on the Police Lines and paid tribute to the police, counter-terrorism department, Special Branch, Rescue 1122, doctors, district administration and the people of Kohat for their courage and resilience, according to an official statement issued here. The chief minister said that the manner in which the security personnel and other responders confronted terrorists during an operation lasting nearly 20 hours was highly commendable. Sympathises with families of police officials, civilians martyred in Kohat blast He said the police personnel and civilians who lost lives while confronting terrorists had made the ultimate sacrifice for the protection of the nation. Mr Afridi said Khyber Pakhtunkhwa had been fighting terrorism continuously since 2004, spanning nearly 22 years, during which the province had lost more than 80,000 lives. He said that the government that came to power in Afghanistan was welcomed with celebrations by the “bogus and imposed” Pakistani rulers but the situation later turned bad. “Our trade [with Afghanistan] has been disrupted; the border has been closed; economic activities in the tribal districts have come to a standstill, and terrorism in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa continues to rise,” he said. The chief minister said the closure of the Afghan border had caused Khyber Pakhtunkhwa losses of more than Rs8 billion during the previous financial year, while the province was likely to face further economic losses during the current financial year. He said if a policy was not delivering results and was continuously failing, there was a need to change it. Mr Afridi said that the people and police of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa continued to bear the immense burden of the fight against terrorism. He said that police personnel remained on the frontline, fighting, sustaining injuries and laying down their lives, while innocent citizens, with no crime or wrongdoing to their name, continued to be killed and injured. The chief minister said despite those sacrifices, the people of the province continued to be viewed in that manner, which was deeply regrettable. Referring to the prevailing state narrative, he said that those imposed on the people were calling them terrorists while claiming that there is no threat from India. Mr Afridi said that the federal government and institutions were trying to suppress PTI’s political activity instead of addressing the challenge of terrorism. He said that while the focus of the federal government and institutions was on such matters, there was little concern for the people who were making sacrifices on the frontline. Addressing the youth, people and police of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the chief minister said that no one else would come to stand with them and that they must stand up for themselves, their people, their province and the country. He urged them to remain steadfast and keep their morale high, noting that the people and police of the province have continued to fight terrorism with courage and determination for the past 22 years without allowing their resolve to break. Mr Afridi announced that financial assistance would also be provided to the families of those martyred in the incident who didn’t fall within the scope of the government’s Shuhada Package. Announcing the provision of modern medical equipment at the District Headquarters Hospital in Kohat, he said that the shortage of CT scan, MRI and other essential modern medical equipment would be addressed. The chief minister said that DHQ hospitals across the province were being revamped and that necessary modern equipment would be provided to the hospital. He also announced the establishment of a police station for the Special Branch in Kohat and said that the project would be completed at the earliest. Mr Afridi said that patient care at the Kohat Police Hospital should be improved with the help of necessary facilities. He also took note of the shortage of police personnel and said that the matter would be taken up in the cabinet for necessary decisions. Earlier, the chief minister visited the Kohat District Headquarters Hospital, met the injured blast victims and wished them speedy recovery. Published in Dawn, September 20th, 2026

articles.title: Pakistan snubs Taliban’s ‘pretence of dialogue’
articles.description: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan on Saturday said it had consistently pursued dialogue and constructive engagement with the Afghan Taliban, but would not allow what it called the “pretence of dialogue” to shield those threatening its people. The information ministry was responding to Afghan Taliban spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid’s remarks in an interview with Al Arabiya English a day earlier, in which he said Afghanistan wanted dialogue with Pakistan and called for stronger mechanisms for intelligence-sharing and cooperation. He also welcomed a larger Saudi role in mediating between Kabul and Islamabad, saying Saudi Arabia was a friend of both countries and could play a “positive role” in resolving their differences. Pakistan also rejected Kabul’s warning of “retaliatory action” if Islamabad carried out military operations inside Afghanistan, saying the Taliban regime should dismantle terrorist networks operating from its territory instead of “deflecting responsibility”. During the interview, Mr Mujahid warned Pakistan against conducting military operations inside Afghanistan and said Kabul would defend its sovereignty against any such action. Responding to Kabul spox seeking talks, Islamabad says Afghan govt should dismantle terrorists operating from its territory He also denied Islamabad’s assertion that Afghan territory was being used by militant groups to launch attacks inside Pakistan. “If Pakistan invokes Article 51 to violate the sanctity of Afghan territory, Afghanistan has the right to defend its country, and we will do so,” he said, warning of a “crushing response” to any violation of Afghan sovereignty. Pakistan reiterated that it had the “will and capability” to eliminate terrorist threats and would take all necessary measures, in accordance with international law, to protect its citizens, territory and sovereignty. Pakistan also linked the Afghan Taliban’s warning to the deadly terrorist attack on civilians and police officials offering Friday prayers in Kohat. “We strongly condemn the barbaric terrorist attack on civilians and police officials offering Friday prayers in Kohat,” the ministry of information stated, describing the attackers as “the vilest of Khwarij with roots in Afghanistan”. It said Pakistan had repeatedly raised concerns over the use of Afghan territory by Fitna al-Khawarij and other terrorist groups to plan and launch attacks inside Pakistan. The state uses the term Fitna al-Khawari j for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP). “The presence of terrorist sanctuaries, alongside their recruitment and support infrastructure in Afghanistan, poses a direct threat to Pakistan’s security,” it said, adding that the concerns had repeatedly been conveyed to the Afghan Taliban regime and its interlocutors. The ministry said the Taliban must dismantle the networks instead of “deflecting responsibility”. Pakistan also rejected Mujahid’s assertion that Kabul did not allow the TTP to operate from Afghan territory or support armed groups targeting other countries. Pakistan said the Afghan Taliban had obligations under the Doha Agreement to prevent Afghan territory from being used to threaten other countries. It said it had noted the Afghan Ministry of Foreign Affairs’ condemnation of the Kohat attack and expression of sympathy for the victims’ families, but regretted that the statement did not mention terrorism. “Condemnation must be matched by concrete action,” the ministry said, calling on the Taliban to take “credible, verifiable and sustained measures” to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries and disrupt recruitment and training networks. Published in Dawn, September 20th, 2026
